content: Next.js 16 App Router route handler streaming: the idiomatic pattern is exactly what cover-letter/route.ts already uses — create a ReadableStream with a start(controller) that enqueues TextEncoder chunks, return new Response(stream, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' } }). This is confirmed in the official Next.js 16.2.9 streaming guide. Client-side: fetch the route, read response.body.getReader(), loop { done, value } = await reader.read(), TextDecoder decode each chunk into state. The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header is recommended but optional. No SSE needed for plain text streaming — SSE adds complexity without benefit for this use case. Vercel supports streaming natively. Safari buffers until 1024 bytes (not a real issue for text responses). Streaming starts only when first chunk is enqueued; status code is locked at 200 once streaming begins — validate inputs before starting the stream.
